meeting_header:
Date: 2027-08-11
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (CTO - LumenAI), Aisha Rahman (ML Eng - LumenAI), Carlos Gomez (DevOps - LumenAI)
summary: Discovery focused on integration patterns for Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Main themes: SDK support (Python/Node), LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy placement, rate limits & quotas, observability hooks and tracing. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private due to PII/data residency concerns; initial pilot on hosted for dev but require compliance docs and TCO before committing.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro from our side — i'm Samir, AE on the account, and Maya is our solutions engineer.
[00:07] Daniel Park: Thanks Samir. Yep, i'm Daniel, CTO at LumenAI. we have Aisha and Carlos on too.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Hi all, nice to meet you. we'll keep this high level then dig into integration details after the context.
[00:20] Aisha Rahman: Great. to set context, we have a product that annotates customer support tickets, extracts entities and suggests responses. currently running inference on-prem (NVIDIA A100s) but want to explore moving to a managed infra to lower ops overhead.
[00:36] Carlos Gomez: We also have strict data residency for EU customers and some PII redaction rules, so whatever we pick needs to satisfy that.
[00:44] Samir Patel: Totally, so our goal for today is to map integration patterns — SDKs, frameworks like LangChain or LlamaIndex, where a gateway would sit, and what observability hooks look like. also cover rate limits/quotas and what Dedicated/Private options would mean for you.
[00:58] Daniel Park: Sounds good. quick question up front — do you have first class support for LangChain and LlamaIndex? we've built a bunch of pipelines around those.
[01:07] Maya Chen: Yes — we have SDKs in Python and Node, and official adapters/examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. i should caveat that some of the community integrations were contributed externally; we maintain an official examples repo with recommended patterns for cacheing and async calls. (audio glitch, slight)
[01:27] Aisha Rahman: By cacheing do you mean prefix kv cache or something else? we really care about reducing token cost.
[01:32] Maya Chen: Exactly. Redwood runtime exposes prefix/KV cache options and you can plug those via the SDK. in LangChain workflows you typically use a cached llm wrapper or store the KV state in a redis-like store. our examples include a small redis pattern and a direct runtime-backed KV cache.
[01:47] Daniel Park: If we use the runtime KV cache, where does the data live? is it in the hosted cluster or in our VPC?
[01:54] Samir Patel: For hosted, cache lives on our managed runtime in the region. for Dedicated, you can opt to have the cache on your dedicated fleet; and for Private (VPC/on-prem) the cache is inside your network. we'll capture exact options but those are the typical placements.
[02:10] Carlos Gomez: OK that helps. we're leaning away from hosted for production because of the PII concerns, but for a dev pilot hosted might be okay.
[02:18] Maya Chen: That's a common pattern — dev on hosted for speed, then pilot to Dedicated or Private for prod workloads.
[02:24] Daniel Park: Let's talk about client integration. we have backend microservices in python and some nodejs workers. ideally we want a simple SDK call from our services, with retries, exponential backoff, and local batching.
[02:35] Maya Chen: Our Python SDK supports sync/async, automatic retries, and has batching primitives. also supports a local batching proxy library you can run as a sidecar — that helps group short requests to reduce latency and tokens.
[02:47] Aisha Rahman: Sidecar sounds interesting. is that the same as your gateway/proxy product or is that something customer-run?
[02:53] Maya Chen: There's two options: you can use Redwood's managed gateway — a hosted proxy layer we operate — or run a lightweight proxy sidecar in your cluster that speaks to our API. the sidecar handles batching, token-level pre/post processing, and metrics emission to your observability.
[03:09] Carlos Gomez: For Private deployment we would run the sidecar together with the runtime, right?
[03:13] Samir Patel: Correct. Private deployments include the control plane but runtime sits in your VPC/on-prem; the sidecar and gateway components are customer-controlled.
[03:20] Daniel Park: What about rate limits/quotas? we have bursts during ticket spikes and need to guarantee throughput.
[03:26] Maya Chen: We expose per-key and per-route rate limits. for Dedicated you get reserved throughput and can configure burst capacity. for hosted tier we have quota tiers — you can request bump during pilot. for private it's controlled by your infra.
[03:38] Aisha Rahman: do you support token-based quotas or minute-based RPS quotas? we care about tokens because that maps to our cost.
[03:44] Maya Chen: Both — you can set token quotas (monthly/weekly) and RPS caps. our console breaks down token usage at the route/model level so you can see per-customer or per-endpoint cost.
[03:54] Daniel Park: observability: we use datadog and jaeger. can we get traces correlated to Redwood requests and token counts?
[04:02] Maya Chen: Yes. we have observability hooks — X-Request-ID propagation, structured telemetry with per-token metrics, and tracing support that exports to Jaeger/OTel-compatible collectors. we also emit logs and span attributes that include model version, latency breakdown, and tokens consumed.
[04:18] Carlos Gomez: how about alerting on model quality regressions? we run evals on production prompts.
[04:24] Samir Patel: Redwood Optimize can run quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. we can surface diffs and hook alerts into Slack or your incident system.
[04:33] Aisha Rahman: nice. about LangChain integration — do you have a specific LLM wrapper that preserves streaming and function-calling? we rely on streaming tokens for UI responsiveness.
[04:45] Maya Chen: Our LangChain adapter preserves streaming and supports function/tool calling semantics. there are a couple of caveats: for older community adapters streaming is sometimes buffered; our maintained adapter is designed to stream at the token level. we'll send the repo link.
[04:59] Daniel Park: LlamaIndex — we currently use LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented pipelines. any gotchas there?
[05:06] Maya Chen: LlamaIndex works fine; recommended pattern is to use a local vector store and call Redwood for the generation step. for RAG you can use our embeddings endpoint or run embedding generation on Dedicated. note on embeddings: for hosted we keep embeddings tenant-scoped; for Private you can control key rotation/KMS.
[05:23] Carlos Gomez: On key rotation, we have strict KMS requirements and hardware-backed keys—HSM. do you support that?
[05:30] Samir Patel: Yes, for Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and key import. Dedicated has integrations with cloud KMS and bring-your-own-key options. we'll share the security docs.
[05:45] Aisha Rahman: one technical thing — we sometimes need to run small local models for latency sensitive paths. can Redwood runtime do hybrid routing? e.g., route short queries to local LLM and fallback to Redwood hosted for complex ones?
[05:57] Maya Chen: We support smart routing policies. you can attach policy based on latency or cost; common setup is local-first for short prompts then fallback to Dedicated/Hosted. routing is pluggable via our control plane.
[06:09] Daniel Park: good. capacity planning — for our SLA we'd need 99.9% for the inference path. do you offer SLAs on Dedicated?
[06:16] Samir Patel: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. hosted has best-effort for lower tiers but higher tiers can have contractual SLAs. Private is governed by the deployment agreement.
[06:28] Carlos Gomez: any sample benchmark data for expected latency on a 2k token generation on A100 vs q4 quantized models?
[06:35] Maya Chen: we have model catalog performance profiles — i'll attach our benchmark spreadsheet. rough numbers: on A100 (fp16) ~250-400ms per 1k tokens for causal models; quantized on T4/V100 variants can be higher latency but lower cost — again we'll share specific curves.
[06:53] Aisha Rahman: that's great. can you also provide an example of the SDK call for streaming in python and how we would hook it into our existing tracing?
[07:01] Maya Chen: absolutely — snippet will include OTel headers and how to forward request ids.
[07:08] Daniel Park: licensing/compliance — is Redwood SOC 2? GDPR-ready? we need vendor paperwork for procurement.
[07:15] Samir Patel: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and maintains GDPR compliance guidance. for Private we can do on-prem + data residency. we'll send SOC 2 report and DPA template to your procurement team.
[07:28] Carlos Gomez: network requirements — what's the egress pattern? do we need specific ports for the sidecar?
[07:33] Maya Chen: sidecar needs outbound to our control plane for management; runtime-host communication for hosted uses HTTPS on 443. for Private there are no outbound egress requirements other than for control plane if you opt in; we'll share a firewall checklist.
[07:49] Aisha Rahman: a small question on costs — do you expose per-token cost in the billing API? we want to show per-customer cost breakdown.
[07:57] Samir Patel: Billing API and Console provide token-level cost attribution and meter by route/model/customer tag. you can export to S3 or push to your billing system.
[08:07] Daniel Park: Ok, i want to understand migration path — initial dev on hosted, then Dedicated pilot, then Private for EU production. timeline wise we're looking at Q4 pilot and Q1 production.
[08:18] Samir Patel: Sounds doable. typical timeline: 2-4 week dev pilot on hosted, Dedicated provisioning takes a few weeks after commitment, Private/on-prem varies with infra readiness.
[08:28] Maya Chen: For the pilot we can provide a templated repo with LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, the sidecar, and a simple benchmark harness.
[08:36] Daniel Park: perfect. any gotchas with LlamaIndex's tokenization differences or output formatting when using streaming? we've seen some truncation in the past.
[08:46] Maya Chen: Truncation usually happens when the client-side buffer flush isn't tuned; our streaming adapter flushes per token but network buffers can chunk. we'll share tuning parameters for the client and examples.
[08:58] Aisha Rahman: Security question again — audit logs and read-only access to logs for third-party auditors, is that possible?
[09:05] Samir Patel: Yes — we provide audit logs and can set RBAC so auditors get read-only access. for Private you can keep logs inside your systems.
[09:14] Carlos Gomez: Are there pre-built dashboards for model-level latency and token breakdown?
[09:18] Maya Chen: Redwood Console has per-route/model dashboards, token-level breakdown, and the ability to create saved views and alerts. you can also forward metrics to datadog.
[09:29] Daniel Park: Great. on auditing, our compliance team will want the SOC2 and encryption details. we'll share contact.
[09:35] Samir Patel: We'll send the SOC2 and our compliance pack.
[09:39] Maya Chen: Quick technical note — for LangChain's Agent APIs, we support function calling semantics and tool invocation; we recommend running the planner and some tool-execution steps in your environment and generation in Redwood to reduce surface area.
[09:53] Aisha Rahman: Makes sense. we also want to instrument a canary to watch for quality regressions during model rollouts. can Redwood do canary rollouts?
[10:01] Maya Chen: Yes, rollouts with canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to previous model versions are supported. hooks for evals and automatic rollback on regression are part of Redwood Optimize.
[10:12] Daniel Park: Awesome. any limitations we should be aware of for very long context windows (>32k)?
[10:18] Maya Chen: We support long context models; the runtime provides K/V streaming and optimized kernels. for extremely long contexts you'd want Dedicated or Private to fine-tune kernel selection and memory.
[10:29] Carlos Gomez: Final question — latency SLOs for Dedicated, are they per-request p95 or p99?
[10:35] Samir Patel: SLAs are typically tied to p95 latency, but we can discuss p99 in enterprise agreements.
[10:42] Daniel Park: Thanks. can we recap next steps?
[10:45] Samir Patel: Sure. i'll send pricing deck and hosted vs dedicated TCO, SOC2 + compliance pack, and the benchmark spreadsheet.
[10:52] Maya Chen: i'll share the LangChain/LlamaIndex example repo, sidecar/proxy config snippets, and a streaming SDK snippet with OTel headers.
[10:59] Carlos Gomez: i'll confirm our firewall and VPC requirements and get back to you.
[11:05] Daniel Park: i'll schedule the infra sync and loop in procurement.
[11:08] Samir Patel: Great. we'll aim to have those artifacts to you by Friday. thanks everyone.
[11:12] Aisha Rahman: Thanks all.
[11:14] End of call.
